Dispatch scope = the card's own suggested rule, landed as one clause in the dispatch-order conventions: *a hazard claim about the code in a dispatch order needs a reading (call sites / paths / migration named), same register as the zero-hit rule; can't measure it from the PM seat ⇒ write it as a question for the dev, not a fence. The human-floor fence (decisions the maintainer owns) is exempt and needs no measurement.* One rule, ceiling paid by compression. Fold-candidate with #11901/#11936/#11724 into a single dispatch-order-discipline amendment PR at dispatch time (same file region, same class — fold decision stays with the dispatching round).

Accepted here because (a) the dev flagged it in the PR body instead of burying it, (b) the re-wrap tool mechanically refused any line present verbatim on origin/main — no ruling quote re-flowed, no untouched paragraph densified, and (c) the six rules are graded, maintainer-era work that must land in a zero-headroom file whose ceiling only the maintainer may raise. **This is a live instance of exactly what #11947 (needs-user-decision) is about** — the line ceiling cannot see byte growth — and it is cross-referenced there as evidence for the A-ratchet option. If the maintainer prefers word-cuts-only funding, the remedy is a follow-up compression pass on this file, named as such in the PR body.

Landing: on merge, five cards close; #11923 stays open on its `Part of` until this PR's sibling (#12082, already ACCEPTed) merges — whichever lands second completes it. `pm:dispatched` off in the merge stroke.
